## 1. Verified narrative

*Reference tree: `/home/coder/chromium-ref/src` at commit `f288fed6c601ae22461c9c9d8189004050abfaeb`, `chrome/VERSION` 156.0.8067.0, checked out 2026-09-18, V8 15.6.0 [src/chrome/VERSION:1-4; v8/include/v8-version.h:11-18]. Live-service readings (Swarming, Buildbucket, CIPD, Gerrit, LUCI Config, Pinpoint) were taken 2026-09-18 → 09-22 and are dated where they appear. Facts cited as URLs were fetched from the GitHub/gitiles mirrors because the file is outside the sparse checkout or outside chromium/src.*

### 1.1 One tree, four pipelines

Chromium's "CI/CD" is not a pipeline but four of them, sharing one substrate. A **pre-submit** pipeline verifies every CL; a **post-submit** pipeline rebuilds and retests every commit on `refs/heads/main`; a **performance** pipeline measures a much smaller set of commits on real hardware; and a **release** pipeline cuts branches, bumps versions, pins dependencies and packages binaries. All four run on LUCI — "a collection of CI services that run on Google Cloud [which] form the backbone of Chromium's CI system" [src/docs/infra/glossary.md:101-102] — and, decisively, all four are *configured from files checked into chromium/src itself*. The glossary fixes the vocabulary: a Build is "A Buildbucket job that runs a single CI-specific task" composed of steps rendered in Milo, a Builder is "A named configuration (or grouping) of builds in Buildbucket", and "As of writing (Q3 2022), all Buildbucket builds are themselves Swarming tasks" [src/docs/infra/glossary.md:10-20]. The 2026 tree still bears that out: every one of the 1,211 builders in the generated Buildbucket config carries `swarming_host: "chromium-swarm.appspot.com"` [src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg], and a Q2-2025 doc raises the claim to "nearly 100% of Chromium infra workloads run as Swarming tasks" [src/docs/infra/builder_types.md:20-32].

### 1.2 The Buildbot inheritance

The present shape is legible only against what it replaced. LUCI ("Layered Universal Continuous Integration") split Buildbot's single-threaded monolithic masters into independent services for scheduling, distribution, collection, archiving and logging; Buildbot "masters" survive only as UI "groups" [src/docs/tour_of_luci_ui.md:279-297]. Migration of Chromium builders began in Q1 2018 [https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/71.0.3578.80/docs/luci_migration_faq.md]; all CQ builders and their waterfall mirrors were on LUCI by 31 May 2018 [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/jXFeC21Aq2A/m/WvzCfqiKAAAJ]; and on 25 September 2019 Eric Foo of Chrome Operations announced under the subject "Chrome is 100% on LUCI. Buildbot officially turned down" that "Yesterday, we officially turned down the last Buildbot master and are now 100% on LUCI (ci.chromium.org) as the official build infrastructure for ChromeOS and Chrome official releases, CI/Waterfall, and CQ/tryjobs systems" [https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/zS3R6IEN7X4/m/gYuWAZYtAQAJ]. Recipes replaced Buildbot's server-side "Build Factories", which pre-computed all steps; a recipe is "a domain-specific language (embedded in Python) for specifying sequences of subprocess calls in a cross-platform and testable way" [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/recipes-py/+/main/README.md]. Fossils remain: `bot_update` still heads the tree-closing step regexp although it can no longer close the tree (§1.10), and `//testing/buildbot` still carries a `waterfalls.pyl` (§1.11).

### 1.3 The tree configures the fleet

`//infra/config` holds "the configuration for the LUCI services (also known as Chrome Operations) for the chromium project", written in Starlark and executed by lucicfg into protobuf-text configs under `generated/` [src/infra/config/README.md:6-25]. At f288fed6 the directory is itself a lucicfg *package*: `PACKAGE.star` declares `@chromium-project` with a minimum lucicfg of 1.44.1, two entry points (`main.star` for production, `dev.star` for the dev instance) and two dependencies — `@chromium-luci`, fetched from the separate `infra/chromium` repo and pinned at revision `3c067cfcf061330718cee8a4c74d9cd7232595c6`, and a local `@chromium-targets` package rooted at `infra/config/targets` [src/infra/config/PACKAGE.star:7-43; PACKAGE.lock:2-9]. That split is the most important structural change of the last two years: on 2025-07-22 commit b711da6e4f deleted the entire `infra/config/lib` library — `builders.star`, `ci.star`, `try.star`, `builder_config.star`, `gn_args.star`, `targets.star`, `bootstrap.star`, `branches.star`, `notifiers.star`, `orchestrator.star` — from chromium/src and replaced it with `load("@chromium-luci//ci.star", "ci")`-style imports, so chromium and the internal chrome project share one library [https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/b711da6e4f]. What remains in `lib/` is project constants: CI defaults (recipe `chromium`, 3-hour timeout, pool `luci.chromium.ci`), try defaults (recipe `chromium_trybot`, 4 hours, `luci.chromium.try`), Siso RBE projects and job tiers, Xcode 27.0 RC `27a266a`, twelve gardener rotations, and grandfathered exemption lists that "should *only* decrease" [src/infra/config/lib/ci_constants.star:5-14; try_constants.star:5-10; siso.star:5-21; xcode.star:7-14; gardener_rotations.star:10-23; builder_exemptions.star:5-11].

`main.star` is the contract. It pins lucicfg, enables the crbug.com/1182002 Scheduler experiment, and calls `lucicfg.config(config_dir = "generated", fail_on_warnings = True)` with an explicit `tracked_files` manifest naming every artefact lucicfg owns: the LUCI service cfgs, the per-builder trees `builders/*/*/*`, `builder-owners/*.txt`, `cq-builders.md`, `cq-usage/*`, `health-specs`, `sheriff-rotations/*.txt`, `outages.pyl`, `project.pyl` and `testing/*.pyl` [src/infra/config/main.star:27-68]. Three files (`testhaus.cfg`, `luci-analysis.cfg`, `luci-bisection.cfg`) are hand-written and merely copied by `lucicfg.emit` [src/infra/config/main.star:70-86]. `luci.project` then binds the hosts — `cr-buildbucket.appspot.com`, `luci-logdog`, `luci-milo`, `luci-notify`, `luci-scheduler`, `chromium-swarm` — and a block of `chromium_luci.configure_*` calls parameterises the shared library, including the OS-dimension overrides that make `LINUX_DEFAULT` mean Ubuntu-22.04, `MAC_DEFAULT` mean Mac-26 and `WINDOWS_DEFAULT` mean Windows-10 [src/infra/config/main.star:88-96,199-211].

The output is large and mechanical. `cr-buildbucket.cfg` is 139,286 lines / 5,544,282 bytes (5.3 MiB, 5.5 MB decimal) holding 18 buckets and 1,211 builders: ci 641, try 500, build 20, webrtc.fyi 14, reviver 12, codesearch 8, webrtc 8, findit 2, infra 2, trusted.robots 2, flaky-reproducer 1, ssci 1, plus six empty dynamic `*.shadow` buckets that exist "for led builds" [src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg; src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/ci.star:73-115]. Alongside it: `commit-queue.cfg` 9,451 lines, `luci-scheduler.cfg` 7,092 lines with 697 jobs and 5 gitiles triggers, `luci-milo.cfg` 31,964 lines with 90 consoles, `luci-notify.cfg` 6,013 lines with 252 notifiers and 133 tree closers, `realms.cfg` 933 lines with 27 realms [src/infra/config/generated/luci/*]. The whole Starlark tree is 125 files and 76,580 lines; `generated/` is 3,555 files and 53 MB. A CI builder is one keyword-argument call: "Linux Builder" names a `builder_spec`, five GN-arg configs, a targets bundle and a console entry, and inherits pool, cores, OS, gardener rotation, tree-closing and timeout from the file's `ci.defaults` [src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/ci/chromium.linux.star:20-44,328-378]. lucicfg expands that into a Buildbucket builder, a Scheduler job, Milo console entries, notify/tree-closer entries, a health spec, an owner line, and four per-builder files — `properties.json`, `shadow-properties.json`, `gn-args.json` and `targets/<group>.json`.

### 1.4 How configuration reaches the services

Nothing is deployed. LUCI Config (Go, `config.luci.app`; the Python `luci-config.appspot.com` was shut down 2024-10-09 and now only JavaScript-redirects) runs an `import-configs` cron: `importAllConfigs` enqueues one task per config set with a deterministic offset inside a 10-minute window, looks the project up in its own `projects.cfg` registry, asks Gitiles for the latest commit touching the configured path, fetches a gzip archive, and only commits the revision if every interested service's `ValidateConfigs` returns no ERROR-severity message [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/config_service/internal/importer/importer.go]. On 2026-09-22 `projects/chromium` was imported from `chromium/src` `refs/heads/main` path `infra/config/generated/luci` at revision f7de74e13efc (2026-09-22T08:25:50Z) with `lastImportAttempt: Up-to-date` [https://config.luci.app/config_set/projects/chromium]. Consumers then poll: Buildbucket's `update_project_config` cron every minute, Scheduler every minute, CV "every minute on average", so a landed `infra/config` CL is normally live within roughly 1–11 minutes, dominated by the import window [luci-go buildbucket/appengine/frontend/cron.yaml:8-11; scheduler/appengine/frontend/cron.yaml:1-4; cv/internal/configs/prjcfg/refresher/cron.go:168-171]. Presubmit runs the same validator earlier: depot_tools' `CheckLucicfgGenOutput` executes `lucicfg validate main.star`, which regenerates, diffs, and ships each config set to the same RPC [depot_tools/presubmit_canned_checks.py:3744-3778]. Four dedicated verifier trybots (`branch-config-verifier`, `builder-config-verifier`, `gn-args-verifier`, `targets-config-verifier`) guard the generated per-builder files [src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/try/presubmit.star:41-176].

### 1.5 How a build actually runs

A Buildbucket build is a Swarming task whose command is its recipe [src/docs/infra/builder_types.md:42-52]. Swarming is "purely a task scheduler service" with "a legion of dumb bots" that poll and are matched by dimensions; a pool is a security boundary and file I/O goes through RBE-CAS, the successor of isolate [src/docs/infra/glossary.md:129-149]. On the bot, `bbagent` runs a LogDog butler, merges `build.proto` datagrams from the luciexe and forwards them to Buildbucket and Milo; a luciexe that exits without a terminal status is treated as INFRA_FAILURE [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/luciexe/doc.go].

The subtle part is *which* code runs. 1,070 of the 1,211 builders do not run a recipe directly: their `exe` is the CIPD package `infra/chromium/bootstrapper/${platform}` at `cipd_version: "latest"`, with the real recipe bundle hidden in the `$bootstrap/exe` property at `refs/heads/main` and the builder's properties named by `$bootstrap/properties`; the other 141 run `cmd: "luciexe"` on the bundle directly [src/infra/config/generated/luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg]. The reason is versioning: the bootstrapper reads a builder's properties file *from the source revision being built*, so a CQ run exercises the property change contained in its own CL, and a build of an old revision gets the properties of that revision [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/chromium/+/main/starlark-libs/chromium-luci/bootstrap.star:5-18]. The bootstrapper even applies the CL's diff to the properties file it reads. One consequence deserves a figure: neither an orchestrator nor the compilator it schedules pins the bundle — `ScheduleBuildRequest.exe` supports only `cipd_version` overrides — so each resolves `refs/heads/main` at its own start and they can run different recipe revisions if a bundle lands in between [chromium_orchestrator/api.py:535-542; buildbucket/proto/builds_service.proto:437-439].

### 1.6 The fleet behind the config

The configuration names pools; Swarming's anonymously readable `CountBots` says what is behind them. On 2026-09-22 (09:45–09:55Z, a Tuesday US night) the builder pools held `luci.chromium.ci` 590 bots (436–438 busy) for 490 declared builders, `luci.chromium.try` 2,113–2,114 bots (584–730 busy) for 382 primary builders, `luci.chromium.gpu.ci` 351 and `luci.chromium.gpu.try` 287 [https://chromium-swarm.appspot.com/prpc/swarming.v2.Bots/CountBots]. The test pools are an order of magnitude bigger and breathe with load: `chromium.tests` read 20,320–20,694 bots at night and 24,172 the previous afternoon, because 13,180 of its bots are GCE VMs managed by the Robocrop autoscaler (documented example: Win10 100–3,700 instances) while 7,395 are physical machines in three Google labs [src/docs/infra/os_upgrade_playbook.md:337-383]. `chromium.tests.gpu` is the opposite shape — 3,266 bots, 3,118 physical, split Intel 548 / NVIDIA 391 / AMD 380 / Apple 370 / Qualcomm 159, with 1,500 Android devices. Throughput in the 24 hours to 2026-09-22T09:59:47Z: `chromium.tests` created 2,417,399 tasks (2,364,471 completed, of which 35,354 with non-zero exit; 210,323 deduped; 545 expired; 139 BOT_DIED; 324 NO_RESOURCE), `chromium.tests.avd` 545,729 and `chromium.tests.gpu` 372,101 [Swarming `Tasks/CountTasks`, re-queried 2026-09-22T12:05-12:10Z]. A surprise for the explainer: `luci.chromium.try` is mostly *builderful* — only 513 of 2,113 bots carry `builderless:1`; the rest are dedicated through a multi-valued `builder:` dimension to 67 named builders (mac-gpu-rel 80, win-libfuzzer-asan-rel 72, win-rel 55, seven iOS builders sharing one 54-machine group). The sample day also caught an incident: 25,921 of 43,933 `luci.chromium.ci` tasks ended NO_RESOURCE, against 150–731 on each of the four preceding days, because Windows-10 builderless bots with `cores:8`/`ssd:0` were reporting `free_space:high` while ci builders request `free_space:standard` [Swarming CountTasks/CountBots; src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/ci.star:20].

### 1.7 The commit path: upload, presubmit, review

A change starts in depot_tools. `git cl upload` runs `presubmit_support.py --upload` and pushes to Gerrit's magic ref `refs/for/<branch>%<opts>`; new changes are WIP unless `--send-mail`, and `-c`/`-d` append `l=Commit-Queue+2` / `+1` as push options [depot_tools/git_cl.py:1935-1996,2210-2253,7205-7218]. `src/PRESUBMIT.py` declares `PRESUBMIT_VERSION = '2.0.0'`, under which presubmit_support runs every global `Check*` function, skipping `*Commit` on upload and `*Upload` on commit [src/PRESUBMIT.py:4-23; depot_tools/presubmit_support.py:1797-1811]. The file is 8,937 lines with 95 top-level checks — banned patterns as `BanRule` dataclasses, `CheckUnwantedDependencies` running checkdeps on newly added includes (errors for `-` rules, warnings for `!`), `CheckNoIOStreamInHeaders`, `CheckTodoBugReferences` (bug ids must exceed the last Monorail id 1524553), `CheckTreeIsOpenOnCommit`, and depot_tools' hard-coded holiday infra-freeze windows bypassable with `Ignore-Freeze` [src/PRESUBMIT.py; depot_tools/presubmit_canned_checks.py:1179-1240]. Two CQ builders re-run the same scripts in the cloud: `linux-presubmit` and `win-presubmit`, recipe `presubmit`, 40-minute build timeout, 8-minute presubmit step timeout, `on_default_cq` and `disable_reuse`; the recipe runs `--commit --skip_canned CheckTreeIsOpen` because CV checks the tree itself, and uploads findings as ResultDB entries that surface in Gerrit [src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/try/presubmit.star:178-220; depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/presubmit/api.py:174-258]. Review gates are Gerrit-side: one committer's Code-Review+1 (two if the author is not a committer), an OWNERS approval per file, `Owners-Override+1` for gardeners and release PMs, and `Bot-Commit+1` from the Rubber Stamper for clean reverts and cherry-picks [src/docs/contributing.md:318-405; src/docs/code_reviews.md:235-313].

### 1.8 The commit queue is LUCI CV

`commit-queue.cfg` has two config groups. `cq` watches `refs/heads/.+` of chromium/src with committers `project-chromium-submit-access` and dry-runners `project-chromium-tryjob-access`, a `tree_status` verifier on chromium-status.appspot.com, and 603 tryjob verifiers; `fallback-cq` (`fallback: YES`) watches every `refs/branch-heads/.*` except the seven active milestone refs and runs one builder, `requires-testing-checker` — 604 verifier entries in the file [src/infra/config/generated/luci/commit-queue.cfg:14-31,9411-9450]. Of the 603, 467 are `includable_only` (reachable only via `Cq-Include-Trybots`), 7 carry `experiment_percentage`, and `cq-builders.md` summarises the human view: 32 required builders (28 chromium + 4 chrome) that "must pass before a CL may land that affects files outside of //docs and //infra/config", 95 optional path-based builders, 7 experimental and two `mega-cq-launcher`s [src/infra/config/generated/cq-builders.md:1-13,87,1078,1119]. Every builder carries default exclusions for `infra/config/.+` and `docs/.+` plus an include for its own generated directory, so a docs-only CL triggers almost nothing while a property edit for one builder does run that builder.

CV's own machinery is now readable from source. Its trigger finder picks the largest Commit-Queue vote, clamps ≥2 to 2, and sets attempt start to the later of vote time and patchset creation; a full run requires a committer and a Gerrit-submittable CL [luci-go cv/internal/gerrit/trigger/trigger.go:66-209; cv/internal/acls/run_create.go:43-225]. Run states are PENDING → RUNNING → WAITING_FOR_SUBMISSION → SUBMITTING → SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELLED, with SUBMITTING uncancellable and a 10-day force-cancel [cv/internal/run/storage.proto:30-73]. Reuse is why CQ+1 → CQ+2 is fast: every tryjob gets a `ReuseKey` = sha256 over (CL id, MinEquivalentPatchset, disable-reuse footer values), and MinEquivalentPatchset survives NO_CHANGE, NO_CODE_CHANGE, MERGE_FIRST_PARENT_UPDATE, TRIVIAL_REBASE and TRIVIAL_REBASE_WITH_MESSAGE_UPDATE — only REWORK starts a new one [cv/internal/tryjob/execute/reuse_common.go:192-220; cv/internal/gerrit/equi.go:24-76]. The default window is `staleTryjobAge = 24h`; since 2026-07-27 CV can instead compare the build's output `Cr-Commit-Position` with the branch tip, and chromium enabled that on 2026-09-18 for exactly one builder, `linux_chromium_compile_dbg_ng`, at `max_commit_distance` 800 on main only [cv/internal/tryjob/execute/reuse_common.go:116-177; src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/try/tryserver.chromium.linux.star:888-891]. A worked example: CL 8423730's dry run at 19:42 on 09-21 was reused 14.4 hours later by the CQ+2 run for 32 of 34 tryjobs; only the two presubmit builders, which set `disable_reuse`, were launched fresh.

### 1.9 Inside a CQ build

`docs/infra/cq.md` states the anatomy: compile the affected suites, run them "(with patch)" as sharded Swarming tasks, retry failed shards identically "(retry shards with patch)", recompile without the CL and rerun the failures "(without patch)", and fail only tests that failed in both patched phases but passed without the patch [src/docs/infra/cq.md:243-262]. The retry ladder exists because "the CQ has roughly ~20,000 unique flaky tests" [src/docs/infra/cq.md:343-352]. The without-patch phase repeats each failing test 10 times with retry limit 0, and only when ≤100 tests need retrying; CI builders instead retry shards with the limit raised to 5 [tools/build chromium_tests/steps.py]. Known-flaky failures are subtracted using LUCI Analysis, which the recipe queries per failing variant and then records as ResultDB `TestExoneration`s with reasons OCCURS_ON_MAINLINE, OCCURS_ON_OTHER_CLS or NOT_CRITICAL [tools/build recipe_modules/test_utils/api.py]. Since Q4 2021 "all tests on Chrome/Chromium builders have their test results uploaded to ResultDB, and nearly all pass-fail decisions on the builders are based on these results" [src/docs/testing/resultdb.md:5-12]; harnesses talk to a local ResultSink started by `rdb stream`, whose address and token arrive through `LUCI_CONTEXT` [src/build/util/lib/results/result_sink.py:31-66]. Structurally, a CQ build is an orchestrator/compilator pair: `linux-rel` runs `chromium/orchestrator` on 2–4 cores, mirrors ci/Linux Builder, Linux Tests, GPU Linux Builder and Linux Release (NVIDIA), and delegates compile and isolate to `linux-rel-compilator` [src/docs/infra/builder_types.md:159-187; src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/try/tryserver.chromium.linux.star:453-499].

### 1.10 bot_update: materialising a checkout

Every build starts with one step named `bot_update`, and it is a three-layer sandwich: the depot_tools recipe module (`BotUpdateApi`, api.py:298), the 1,458-line resource script `bot_update.py`, and depot_tools proper (`git_cache.py`, `gclient.py`/`gclient_scm.py`) [depot_tools/recipes/recipe_modules/bot_update/api.py:5,298]. The script decides whether the requested revision is a pin, runs `git cache populate` against the bare mirror in `[CACHE]/git` (bootstrapped from `gs://chromium-git-cache/v2/...` when missing or over-packed), then `git clone --no-checkout --local --shared` from that mirror, `git fetch origin <pin>`, `git checkout --force`, `git clean -dff` [bot_update.py:766-858; depot_tools/git_cache.py:251-434]. It writes a `.gclient` pointing at the same cache and runs `gclient sync --verbose --reset --force --upstream --nohooks --noprehooks --delete_unversioned_trees --revision src@unmanaged`: `unmanaged` tells gclient the root is already positioned, and `--nohooks` defers DEPS hooks to a separate `gclient runhooks` step so checkout failures (infra) stay distinguishable from hook failures (product) [bot_update.py:441-483,960-990]. On try builds the recipe passes `--patch_ref <repo>@<target_ref>:<fetch_ref>`; `apply_patch_ref` cherry-picks `target..patch --keep-redundant-commits` and then soft-resets to the base, which is exactly why `got_revision` on a try build is the base commit and not the CL [depot_tools/gclient_scm.py:595-616,812-816]. Patch failures exit 88 and become a red FAILURE with `do_not_retry=true`; `bot_update (without patch)` re-pins every fixed revision and reruns with `patch=False`, which is what makes DEPS-changing CLs deapply correctly [bot_update/api.py:732-790,997-1027]. Since November 2025 the same call also creates a TurboCI `CHECK_KIND_SOURCE` check that the compile check depends on [bot_update/api.py:80-295].

### 1.11 What runs, where, on how many machines

Test configuration is mid-migration between two generations. The legacy generation is `//testing/buildbot`: `waterfalls.pyl`, `test_suite_exceptions.pyl` (which by design can only remove or modify, never add) and a 2,625-line `generate_buildbot_json.py` that expands them into one JSON per waterfall, with a documented layering order and `$$MAGIC_SUBSTITUTION_` hooks for GPU ids and CrOS filter files [src/testing/buildbot/README.md:29-90,465-519; generate_buildbot_json.py:735-864]. The newer generation is Starlark: since 2023-04 the four non-builder-specific pyl files are generated by lucicfg from `//infra/config/targets` into `generated/testing`, and since 2024-01 builders can set `targets = targets.bundle(...)` directly, so only 16 builder groups and 104 machines remain legacy [src/infra/config/targets/README.md:114-141; src/testing/buildbot/waterfalls.pyl]. The targets package is 20,113 lines: tests.star 485 declarations, bundles 368, binaries 329, mixins 215, basic_suites 88, compile_targets 77, variants 55. MB (`//tools/mb/mb.py`) bridges builder identity to GN: it now consults `gn_args_locations.json` and the Starlark-generated `gn-args.json` first, falling back to `mb_config.pyl` (down to 26 groups / 180 builders / 92 configs / 104 mixins), writes `args.gn`, maps swarming targets to GN labels through `gn_isolate_map.pyl` (408 entries), and emits `.isolate` files the recipe archives to CAS [src/tools/mb/mb.py:1213-1348; mb_config.pyl:16-23]. Sharding is environmental — tasks are named `<name>:<index>:<count>` with `GTEST_SHARD_INDEX`/`GTEST_TOTAL_SHARDS`, and the Test Executable API requires runners to execute every test *i* with *i* mod N == M [src/docs/testing/test_executable_api.md:311-328]. Shard counts are then *overridden* by a bot: the `autosharder` builder (bucket `infra`, daily 09:00 UTC) queries 14 days of p80 shard runtimes from BigQuery with ≥1,500 samples, computes `optimal = ceil(shards × (runtime − overhead) / (15 min − overhead))` floored at 1, rewrites `infra/config/autoshard_exceptions.json` and uploads a rubber-stamped auto-submit CL [tools/build recipes/chromium/autosharder.py:96-179; src/infra/config/subprojects/infra/subproject.star:73-113]. This is why the same suite has two numbers: `browser_tests` on ci/Linux Tests is `shards = 20` in Starlark and 70 in the generated spec [src/infra/config/subprojects/chromium/ci/chromium.linux.star:681-696; autoshard_exceptions.json:109-121].

### 1.12 From green to `refs/heads/main`

Between a green CQ+2 run and the commit sit three machines. CV owns the Run; Gerrit owns the merge (chromium/src's submit type is REBASE_ALWAYS with content merge inherited on); the git-numberer Gerrit plugin owns numbering [https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/projects/chromium%2Fsrc/config]. `OnReadyForSubmission` acquires a per-LUCI-project SubmitQueue — one datastore entity with a Current run, a FIFO waitlist and a History of recent submissions — then checks the tree; OPEN and THROTTLED both count as open, a closed tree releases the slot and pokes after a minute, and more than 10 minutes of status-service errors fails the Run [cv/internal/run/impl/handler/submit.go:52-184; cv/internal/run/impl/submit/queue.go:38-90]. Burst pacing lives in that queue: chromium sets `submit_max_burst = 2` with a one-minute delay, and over 400 consecutive main commits no three CV-committed commits fell inside 60 seconds — the only 3-in-60s windows each contained a direct human submit [src/infra/config/main.star:144-149; gitiles log analysis 2026-09-21/22]. Submission is Gerrit `SubmitRevision` per CL with 10 exponential retries; 409 FailedPrecondition is permanent and produces the familiar "Cannot rebase … could not be rebased due to a conflict during merge" message with the CQ vote removed [cv/internal/run/impl/submit/submitter.go:224-347]. REBASE_ALWAYS matters for more than history shape: Gerrit only invokes ChangeMessageModifier plugins for the Rebase Always and Cherry Pick strategies, so numbering only works because the commit is rewritten [gerrit Documentation/dev-plugins.txt]. git-numberer's rule is three lines — at most one parent P, P carries `Cr-Commit-Position: refs/foo/bar@{#X}`, the child carries `@{#X+1}` — with a different-ref case emitting `@{#1}` plus `Cr-Branched-From`, and a validator that rejects merge commits, non-fast-forwards and wrong lineage on every push and submit [https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/gerrit-plugins/git-numberer/+/refs/heads/main/README.md:11-18]. Sequential numbering therefore follows from CV's single submitter plus ref-update atomicity plus the validator — there is no numbering daemon. Auto-Submit is likewise not a CV feature: the `chromium-behavior` Gerrit frontend plugin rewrites a reviewer's Code-Review+1 into CR+1 *and* CQ+2 when Auto-Submit+1 is set, and the Rubber Stamper does the same from the bot side [infra/gerrit-plugins/chromium-behavior web/autosubmit.ts:225-298].

### 1.13 Post-submit: waterfall, tree, gardeners, bisection

`chromium-gitiles-trigger` polls `chromium/src` `refs/heads/main` and fans every commit out to 386 CI builders; the rest of the 641 are triggered by their parents from inside the recipe, via a scheduler `GitilesTrigger` carrying `parent_got_*` properties and `deps_revision_overrides` [src/infra/config/generated/luci/luci-scheduler.cfg:6647-7039; tools/build chromium_tests/api.py trigger_child_builds]. 133 of those builders are tree closers: LUCI Notify closes the tree when a *failing step* matches `\b(bot_update|compile|gclient runhooks|generate_build_files|runhooks|update|\w*nocompile_test)\b` [src/infra/config/notifiers.star:85-125]. Notify only reacts to builds that end SUCCESS or FAILURE, and since `bot_update` runs with `infra_step=True` a broken checkout is a purple INFRA_FAILURE that cannot close the tree — in practice `gclient runhooks` does [luci_notify/notify/notify.go:302-426; bot_update/api.py:309]. Closure is automated in both directions: manually closed trees are never reopened by bots, automatically closed ones reopen when all closers pass or a culprit revert lands [luci_notify/notify/tree_status.go]. The humans are twelve gardener rotations (chromium 141 builders, chromium.gpu 94, dawn 56, chromium.clang 46, android 43, …), renamed from "sheriffs" in May 2023, whose job is to keep the tree open and who may revert with Owners-Override plus Rubber Stamper [src/infra/config/generated/sheriff-rotations/*.txt; src/docs/gardener.md:3-63]. The automation beside them is LUCI Bisection, "formerly GoFindit … the rewrite in Golang of the Python2 version of Findit": nth-section bisection and culprit verification on `findit/gofindit-culprit-verification` and `findit/test-single-revision`, allowed to create 10 reverts a day and auto-submit 4 for compile failures whose culprit is younger than 21,600 s, voting Owners-Override+1, Bot-Commit+1 and Commit-Queue+2; test-failure reverts are created but never submitted [src/infra/config/luci-bisection.cfg:4-68]. It refuses autoroller authors, `NOAUTOREVERT=true`, culprits with merged dependents, and builders without a gardener rotation [luci-go bisection/culpritaction/revertculprit/createrevert.go].

### 1.14 The performance pipeline

Performance CI is a separate system with its own project, scheduling shape, dashboard and bisector. It runs in the internal `chrome` project, whose console and Buildbucket API refuse anonymous callers, so the only public enumeration is src-side: `testing/buildbot/chromium.perf.json` (71 entries: 18 `*-builder-perf`, 46 testers, 7 `*-processor-perf`), `chromium.perf.pinpoint.json`, `perf_lab_platforms.md` (39 primary platforms) and `tools/perf/public_builders.json` — all generated by `tools/perf/generate_perf_data` [src/docs/speed/perf_waterfall.md:17-42; src/testing/buildbot/chromium.perf.json]. Builders build every commit and POST each isolate's CAS digest to Pinpoint's `/api/isolate` so bisects can reuse waterfall builds; testers are one continuously running job per platform covering "the set of commits from the end commit of the previous invocation to the latest built commit", fanned over shards by `perf_device_trigger.py`, which implements soft device affinity. Summed over 46 testers the lab exposes 628 shards. Results are merged by `process_perf_results.py` and uploaded to `chromeperf.appspot.com/add_histograms` and, with `--upload-skia-json`, to GCS for the new Skia Perf dashboard. The dashboard is in transition: the legacy App Engine chromeperf still runs the anomaly detector (max_window_size 50, min_relative_change 0.10, multiple_of_std_dev 2.5) and the alert-group workflow (20-minute batching, 7-day active window, sandwich verification, then auto-bisection), while Skia Perf serves the public `perf.luci.app` [catapult dashboard/dashboard/common/defaults.py:17-27; models/alert_group_workflow.py]. Pinpoint binds Quests to Changes, compares adjacent Changes statistically and expands DEPS to descend into V8 or Skia. Enforcement is social, not a required builder — except for size: `android-binary-size` (16 KB arm32 / 64 KB arm64 / 50 dex methods), `compile-size` (200 MiB) and `fuchsia-binary-size` are `cq: required`, bypassable only with a `Binary-Size:`/`Compile-Size:` footer [src/docs/speed/binary_size/android_binary_size_trybot.md:27-30]. A newer, non-blocking layer is "Perf on CQ": two 100 %-experimental chrome-internal verifiers, `linux-perf-trigger` and `win-perf-trigger`, create Pinpoint try jobs tagged `origin: CQ` with 16 attempts; the experiment started 2025-07-08 and in 35 hours of 2026-09-19/22 the automation account created 539 CQ Perf jobs, 142 Regression Verification jobs and 19 Auto-Bisections.

### 1.15 Releasing the CI system itself

The CI system is "released" by three independent propagation paths, none of them a deploy. (a) **Recipes.** Every commit to `chromium/tools/build` becomes a CIPD bundle: an internal builder running `recipe_bundler` does `recipes.py fetch`, `recipes.py bundle --destination`, then `cipd create -install-mode copy -tag git_revision:<sha> -ref <ref>`, and re-runs `cipd set-ref` even when the tag exists, so any hand-moved ref is undone on the next run [infra/infra go/src/infra/tools/recipe_bundler/cmd_bundle.go:294-393]. Measured over the 12 newest instances the commit-to-CIPD latency is 0.7–4.2 minutes. Only `refs/heads/main` still moves; the 479 `refs/heads/chromium/NNNN` refs were last touched 2020-11-16, which is why branch projects run trunk recipes with branch-pinned properties. Upstream pins move by the recipe autoroller on a 10-minute cadence (163 roll CLs in 30 days, 122 merged, 41 abandoned after a CQ failure); `recipes.py autoroll` tries candidates biggest-first with `test run` (trivial) then smallest-first with `test train` (nontrivial), and tools/build makes trivial rolls self-approving while nontrivial ones wait hours for an owner. (b) **Configs**, as in §1.4. (c) **Binaries.** The bootstrapper is Go in infra/infra packaged for 7 platforms; internal `infra-packager-*` builders upload with `-ref latest`, and because the build is reproducible an unchanged binary re-registers as the *same* instance — the current linux-amd64 `latest` carries 210 `luci_build`/`git_revision` tag pairs, so `latest` moves only when the bytes change, with no canary or promotion. bbagent is the exception: Buildbucket pins it in service settings with a separate `version_canary` selected for canary builds, which chromium's try bucket sets at `task_template_canary_percentage = 5`.

### 1.16 The release cycle and the branches

The single biggest 2026 fact is cadence. `docs/process/release_cycle.md`, rewritten 2026-08-26, now describes two weeks of development on main, a branch, three weeks of stabilisation, then stable, with weekly stable refreshes; Extended Stable maintains every *fourth* milestone for six extra weeks, so a new ES milestone still ships every eight weeks [src/docs/process/release_cycle.md:8-26]. Google announced the change on 2026-03-03 and it took effect with Chrome 153's stable release on 2026-09-08 [https://developer.chrome.com/blog/chrome-two-week-release]. chromiumdash shows the seam: M152 branched 2026-07-27 and shipped 08-25 on the old rhythm; M153 branched 08-17, shipped 09-08; then M154, M155, M156 every two weeks. Versioning is fully verifiable from git. `chrome/VERSION` is four `KEY=VALUE` lines; on trunk BUILD is bumped twice on weekdays (≈03:01 and 14:01 UTC) by `chrome-official-brancher@chops-service-accounts` with "This is an automated release commit … NOAUTOREVERT=true"; the MAJOR bump *is* branch day, which is why a milestone's branch number equals the last trunk BUILD of that milestone (M155 = 8059) [https://github.com/chromium/chromium/commit/3aec864caff1]. Every trunk BUILD number gets its own `refs/branch-heads/NNNN` whose commit @{#1} is "Create chrome_branch_deps.json for branch NNNN." and whose @{#2} is "Incrementing VERSION to X.0.NNNN.1". On branches, PATCH increments via "Incrementing VERSION" commits carrying `Merge-Approval-Bypass: Chrome release infra`, DEPS advance via "Roll commits from side projects in M155", and each stable rollout ships two builds differing only in PATCH for A/B measurement. Branch day is also a config event: `chrome-branch-day@chops-service-accounts` lands "Activate chromium M155" on main (adding the milestone to `milestones.json`) and "Update LUCI config for M155" on the branch (rewriting `settings.json` to project `chromium-m155`, ref `refs/branch-heads/8059`, `is_main` false, seven beta/stable platforms) — after which the branch's generated config holds 256 builders in 30,255 lines against trunk's 1,211 in 139,286, because every builder carries a `branch_selector` the shared `branches.star` matches against the project's platforms [src/infra/config/scripts/branch-day.py:5-21; src/infra/config/milestones.json]. Merges are main-first: a `Merge-Request` field on the bug, a Merge Request issue created within the hour, release managers answering within two business days, then a Gerrit Cherry Pick or `git cl cherry-pick --branch=refs/branch-heads/####` [src/docs/process/merge_request.md].

### 1.17 The release scripts

The scripts themselves are small, old and deliberately boring. V8's live in `v8/tools/release/`: `common_includes.py` (Copyright 2013) gives every script a list of `Step` classes, a JSON state file so `-s N` can resume, retry wait-plans for git, and a regex reader for the four `#define` lines in `include/v8-version.h` [v8/tools/release/common_includes.py:283-562]. `create_release.py` is the daily push — take lkgr, compute build+1/patch 0, push that revision as `refs/heads/<x.y.z>`, rewrite the version header, un-comment the `v8-merges@` WATCHLIST entry, land with `git cl land --bypass-hooks -f`, tag. Rolling into Chromium is two-stage: `detect_roll_candidate` picks the newest version that has a matching `-pgo` tag and force-pushes it to `refs/heads/roll`, and Skia's `v8-chromium-autoroll` (strategy BATCH) turns that into "Roll V8 from A to B" CLs. Back-merges go through Gerrit's REST API rather than local git (`merge_to_branch_gerrit.py`, `roll_merge_gerrit.py`), and patch-level bumps on milestone branches are automated by `auto_tag_ng`. On the Chromium side `build/util/version.py` substitutes `@KEY@` placeholders from VERSION/BRANDING/LASTCHANGE into templates and derives Android Play Store versionCodes; `build/util/lastchange.py`, run as a DEPS hook, writes `LASTCHANGE=<hash>-<Cr-Commit-Position>`, using a dummy all-zero value for non-official builds so they stay reproducible [src/build/util/version.py:34-66; lastchange.py:153-188; lastchange.gni:5-16]. Packaging is mostly vestigial — `FILES.cfg` is obsolete, replaced by `infra/archive_config/*.json` — except on Windows, where `create_installer_archive.py` stages `chrome.release`, builds `chrome.7z`, compresses it with hand-tuned 7z BCJ2/LZMA flags (or a bsdiff/Zucchini differential patch), packs `setup.ex_` with a cross-platform `makecab.py`, and emits `packed_files.rc` [src/chrome/tools/build/win/create_installer_archive.py:71-554]. Toolchain rolls are a third genre: `upload_revision.py` rewrites CLANG_REVISION and the Rust revisions, fires eight `*_upload_clang`/`*_upload_rust` trybots, which run `package.py --upload` into a staging GCS bucket with `x-goog-if-generation-match:0` so nothing is ever overwritten; a Googler promotes, then `sync_deps.py` rewrites the GCS DEPS entries [src/tools/clang/scripts/upload_revision.py; package.py:118-152; src/docs/updating_clang.md:14-62].

### 1.18 The edges

Ten of the eighteen buckets are small and specialised, and they show what the platform is used for beyond building Chrome. `reviver` (12 builders) rebuilds CI targets off-peak and runs their *disabled* tests with `run_disabled=True`, exporting to BigQuery so passing tests can be re-enabled. `flaky-reproducer` (1) applies repeat/batch/parallel strategies to a flaky task and verifies the best reproducing step on CQ builders. `ssci` (1) triggers Crowbar third-party vendoring workflows. `build` (20) measures Siso/RBE build performance and keeps `siso/denylist.star` exhaustive. `codesearch` (8) compiles with Kythe extractors but returns before the kzip upload, making it a pre-submit check that indexing still builds. `trusted.robots` (2, added 2026-06-16) requests Clang builds inside the Lexan trusted-build instance. `infra` (2) is the autosharder and its tester. `findit` (2) is LUCI Bisection's rerun fleet. `webrtc`/`webrtc.fyi` (8 + 14) test WebRTC inside Chromium. Two 2026 rollouts cut across everything: TurboCI, whose `luci.buildbucket.run_in_turboci` experiment is at 100 % on 234 builders and whose SOURCE/BUILD checks the recipes now create, and GardenerAI, which the tree-closure e-mail template says "is currently attempting to identify and revert the culprit" before a human is paged.

```text
            tree_status_host = tree_status_host,
            **kwargs
```

```text
def TryInitClient():

class ResultSinkClient(object):
    def __init__(self, context):
        base_url = 'http://%s/prpc/luci.resultsink.v1.Sink' % context['address']
        self.test_results_url = base_url + '/ReportTestResults'
        self.report_artifacts_url = base_url + '/ReportInvocationLevelArtifacts'
        self.update_invocation_url = base_url + '/UpdateInvocation'

        headers = {

            'Authorization': 'ResultSink %s' % context['auth_token'],
```

```text
def _buildbucket_batch(
    buildbucket_host: str,
    /,
    searches: Sequence[_BuildbucketSearchRequest] = (),
    schedules: Sequence[_BuildbucketScheduleBuildRequest] = (),
) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
    """Calls buildbucket.v2.Builds/Batch via bb and returns parsed json."""
    requests = []
    for s in searches:
        requests.append({"searchBuilds": s})
    for s in schedules:
        requests.append({"scheduleBuild": s})

    (out_str, err_str), returncode = subprocess2.communicate(
        ["bb", "batch", "-host", buildbucket_host],
        stdin=json.dumps({"requests": requests}),
```

### X34. `src/infra/config/validators/builders-in-consoles.star`:5-29

*Shows (IC):* A lucicfg generator used as a validator: fail generation if any builder is missing from every milo console.

```text
def _validate_builders_in_console(ctx):
    builders = {}

    for console in ctx.output["luci/luci-milo.cfg"].consoles:
        for builder in console.builders:
            _, long_bucket, builder_name = builder.name.split("/")
            _, _, bucket = long_bucket.split(".", 2)
            builders.setdefault(bucket, {})[builder_name] = True

    builders_without_console = []

    for bucket in ctx.output["luci/cr-buildbucket.cfg"].buckets:
        if not proto.has(bucket, "swarming"):
            continue
        bucket_builders = builders.get(bucket.name, {})
        for builder in bucket.swarming.builders:
            if builder.name not in bucket_builders:
                builders_without_console.append(
                    "{}/{}".format(bucket.name, builder.name),
                )

    if builders_without_console:
        fail("The following builders do not appear in any console:\n  " +
             "\n  ".join([repr(b) for b in builders_without_console]))
```

```text
def _disable_cq_experiments(ctx):
    if not config.disable_cq_experiments:
        return

    for c in ctx.output["luci/commit-queue.cfg"].config_groups:
        if c.verifiers.tryjob == cq_pb.Verifiers.Tryjob():
            # Accessing the tryjob field where it wasn't set causes it to be set
            # to an empty message and added to the output
            c.verifiers.tryjob = None
            continue
        for b in c.verifiers.tryjob.builders:
            if not b.experiment_percentage:
                continue
            project, bucket, _ = b.name.split("/", 2)
            if project == "chromium" and bucket == "try":
                b.includable_only = True
                b.experiment_percentage = 0
                b.location_filters.clear()

lucicfg.generator(_disable_cq_experiments)
```

```text
def thin_tester(
        *,
        name,
        parent,
        cores = args.DEFAULT,
        **kwargs):
    """Define a thin tester.

    A thin tester is a builder that is triggered by another builder to trigger
    and wait for tests that were built by the triggering builder. Because these
    builders do not perform compilation and are performing platform-agnostic
    operations, they can generally run on small linux machines.

    Args:
        name: The name of the builder.
        parent: Reference to the parent builder.
        cores: See `builders.builder` for more information. The
            `thin_tester_cores` module-level default in `ci.defaults` will be
            used as the default if it is set.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments to forward on to `ci.builder`.

    Returns:
        The `luci.builder` keyset.
    """
```

### X40. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/chromium/+/refs/heads/main/starlark-libs/chromium-luci/try.star`:419-443

*Shows (IC):* chromium-luci's presubmit_builder: forces disable_reuse and drops default path filters so presubmit-style builders always rerun.

```text

    Presubmit builders are builders that run fast checks that don't require
    building. Their results aren't re-used because they tend to provide guards
    against generated files being out of date, so they MUST run quickly so that
    the submit after a CQ dry run doesn't take long.

    Args:
        name: The builder to define.
        cq_settings: An optional try_.cq_settings controlling when the builder is
            added to the CQ. If disable_reuse isn't set, it will be set to
            True. The add_default_filters value will be forced to False.
        **kwargs: Additional keyword args to forward to try_.builder.

    Returns:
        The lucicfg keyset for the builder, None if the builder wasn't defined
        (e.g. branch selector doesn't match current project's settings).
    """

    if cq_settings:
        cq_settings_args = {a: getattr(cq_settings, a) for a in dir(cq_settings)}
        if cq_settings_args.get("disable_reuse") == None:
            cq_settings_args["disable_reuse"] = True
        cq_settings_args["add_default_filters"] = False
        cq_settings = try_.cq_settings(**cq_settings_args)
    return try_builder(name = name, cq_settings = cq_settings, **kwargs)
```

### X43. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/recipes_py/bundle.go`:458-483 (err case elided)

*Shows (CH):* Exact inclusion rules of a recipe bundle: expectation JSON dropped, recipes.cfg kept, `recipes` gitattribute overrides, then recipes/**, recipe_modules/**, recipe_proto/**/*.proto

```text
func (bi *bundleInclusion) shouldInclude(p string) (bool, error) {
	// exclude all the json expectations
	if path.Ext(p) == ".json" && strings.HasSuffix(path.Dir(p), ".expected") {
		return false, nil
	}
	if p == bi.cfgPath {
		return true, nil // always keep recipes.cfg
	}
	match, _ := gitattributes.NewMatcher(bi.gitAttrs).Match(strings.Split(p, "/"), []string{recipesAttrName})
	switch attr, ok := match[recipesAttrName]; {
	case !ok:
	case attr.IsSet():
		return true, nil
	case attr.IsUnset():
		return false, nil
	}

	for _, pat := range bi.patterns {
		switch matched, err := doublestar.Match(pat, p); {
		case matched:
			return true, nil
		}
	}
	return false, nil
```

### X50. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/config_service/internal/importer/importer.go`:520-543

*Shows (CH):* The validation gate: a single ERROR from any consuming service blocks the revision from becoming live

```text
func (i *Importer) validateAndPopulateAttempt(ctx context.Context, cfgSet config.Set, files []*model.File, attempt *model.ImportAttempt) error {
	vfs := make([]validation.File, len(files))
	for i, f := range files {
		vfs[i] = f
	}
	vr, err := i.Validator.Validate(ctx, cfgSet, vfs)
	if err != nil {
		return errors.Fmt("validating config set %q: %w", cfgSet, err)
	}
	attempt.Success = true // be optimistic
	attempt.Message = "Imported"
	attempt.ValidationResult = vr
	for _, msg := range attempt.ValidationResult.GetMessages() {
		switch sev := msg.GetSeverity(); {
		case sev >= cfgcommonpb.ValidationResult_ERROR:
			attempt.Success = false
			attempt.Message = "Invalid config"
			return nil
		case sev == cfgcommonpb.ValidationResult_WARNING:
			attempt.Message = "Imported with warnings"
		}
	}
	return nil
}
```

```text
def _disable_cq_experiments(ctx):
    if not config.disable_cq_experiments:
        return

    for c in ctx.output["luci/commit-queue.cfg"].config_groups:
        if c.verifiers.tryjob == cq_pb.Verifiers.Tryjob():
            # Accessing the tryjob field where it wasn't set causes it to be set
            # to an empty message and added to the output
            c.verifiers.tryjob = None
            continue
        for b in c.verifiers.tryjob.builders:
            if not b.experiment_percentage:
                continue
            project, bucket, _ = b.name.split("/", 2)
            if project == "chromium" and bucket == "try":
                b.includable_only = True
                b.experiment_percentage = 0
                b.location_filters.clear()

lucicfg.generator(_disable_cq_experiments)
```

### X83. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/luci_notify/notify/tree_status.go`:updateTree state-machine comment

*Shows (CP):* LUCI Notify's automatic tree open/close state machine

```text
// State                | Transitions
// ==================== | ========================
// Manually Closed      | Always leave unchanged.
// Manually Opened      | Transition to automatically closed if a (tree-closer)
//                      | build which started after BOTH the manual re-opening AND
//                      | the last automated revert (if any) fails.
// Automatically Closed | Transition to automatically opened if:
//                      |   (1) all (tree-closer) builds pass, OR
//                      |   (2) all failing builds started before the last automated
//                      |       revert (if any) or manual reopen (if any).
// Automatically Opened | Transition to automatically closed if a (tree-closer)
//                      | build is failing and the build started after the last
//                      | automated revert (if any) landed.
```

### X84. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/cv/internal/tryjob/execute/reuse_common.go`:46-86

*Shows (SM):* The three-valued reuse decision and the 24 h default window (panic/UNSPECIFIED cases elided)

```text
// staleTryjobAge is the age after which a Tryjob is too old to reuse.
const staleTryjobAge time.Duration = 24 * time.Hour

type reusability int

const (
	reuseAllowed reusability = iota + 1
	reuseMaybe
	reuseDenied
)

func (w *worker) canReuseTryjob(ctx context.Context, tj *tryjob.Tryjob, mode run.Mode, def *tryjob.Definition) reusability {
	switch status := tj.Status; {
	case status == tryjob.Status_PENDING:
		return reuseMaybe
	case status == tryjob.Status_TRIGGERED && !w.evaluateReuseWindow(ctx, tj, def):
		return reuseDenied
	case status == tryjob.Status_TRIGGERED:
		return reuseMaybe
	case status == tryjob.Status_ENDED && w.canReuseResult(ctx, tj, mode, def):
		return reuseAllowed
	case status == tryjob.Status_ENDED:
		return reuseDenied
	case status == tryjob.Status_CANCELLED:
		return reuseDenied
```

```text
func (w *worker) evaluateReuseWindow(ctx context.Context, tj *tryjob.Tryjob, def *tryjob.Definition) bool {
	if maxDist := def.GetReuseWindow().GetMaxCommitDistance(); maxDist > 0 {
		reusable, err := w.verifyCommitDistance(ctx, tj, maxDist)
		if err == nil {
			return reusable
		}
		logging.Warningf(ctx, "Commit distance verification failed for tryjob %d: %s; falling back to time-based reuse window", tj.ID, err)
	}
	return !isTryjobStale(ctx, tj)
}
```

### X86. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/cv/internal/tryjob/execute/reuse_common.go`:194-220 (sort.Slice collapsed to one line)

*Shows (SM):* The reuse key: CL id + MinEquivalentPatchset + disable_reuse footer values; identical across trivial rebases

```text
func computeReuseKey(cls []*run.RunCL, disableReuseFooters []string) string {
	disableReuseFooterSet := stringset.NewFromSlice(disableReuseFooters...)
	clPatchsets := make([][]byte, len(cls))
	for i, cl := range cls {
		hashInputs := []string{
			fmt.Sprintf("%d", cl.ID),
			fmt.Sprintf("%d", cl.Detail.GetMinEquivalentPatchset()),
		}
		var footers []*changelist.StringPair
		for _, f := range cl.Detail.Metadata {
			if disableReuseFooterSet.Has(f.Key) {
				footers = append(footers, f)
			}
		}
		sortFooters(footers)
		for _, f := range footers {
			hashInputs = append(hashInputs, fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", f.Key, f.Value))
		}
		clPatchsets[i] = []byte(strings.Join(hashInputs, "/"))
	}
	sort.Slice(clPatchsets, func(i, j int) bool { return bytes.Compare(clPatchsets[i], clPatchsets[j]) < 0 })
	h := sha256.New()
	h.Write(bytes.Join(clPatchsets, []byte{0}))
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
}
```

```text
func (c *Cancellator) fetchCandidates(ctx context.Context, clid common.CLID, prevMinEquiPS, curMinEquiPS int32) ([]*tryjob.Tryjob, error) {
	q := datastore.NewQuery(tryjob.TryjobKind).
		Gte("CLPatchsets", tryjob.MakeCLPatchset(clid, prevMinEquiPS)).
		Lt("CLPatchsets", tryjob.MakeCLPatchset(clid, curMinEquiPS))
	var candidates []*tryjob.Tryjob
	for tj, err := range datastore.RunQuery[*tryjob.Tryjob](ctx, q).Results {
		if err != nil {
			return nil, transient.Tag.Apply(errors.Fmt("failed to run the query to fetch candidate tryjobs for cancellation: %w", err))
		}
		switch {
		case tj.ExternalID == "":
			// Most likely Tryjob hasn't been triggered in the backend yet.
		case tj.IsEnded():
		case tj.LaunchedBy == "":
			// Not launched by LUCI CV, may be through `git cl try` command line.
		case tj.Definition.GetSkipStaleCheck():
		default:
			candidates = append(candidates, tj)
		}
	}
```

### X90. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/cv/internal/run/impl/submit/queue.go`:75-90

*Shows (SM):* The burst limiter behind chromium's 2-per-60 s submission pacing

```text
// nextSubmissionETA computes the eta of when next submission can happen based
// on SubmitOptions and submission history.
//
// `now` will be returned verbatim if submission can happen immediately.
func (q *queue) nextSubmissionETA(now time.Time) time.Time {
	switch maxBurst, burstDelay := int(q.Opts.GetMaxBurst()), q.Opts.GetBurstDelay().AsDuration(); {
	case maxBurst <= 0 || burstDelay <= 0:
		return now
	case len(q.History) < maxBurst:
		return now
	case q.History[len(q.History)-maxBurst].After(now.Add(-1 * burstDelay)):
		return q.History[len(q.History)-maxBurst].Add(burstDelay)
	default:
		return now
	}
}
```

### X91. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/luci/luci-go/+/main/cv/internal/run/impl/handler/submit.go`:123-183 (condensed; comments inlined)

*Shows (SM):* Queue slot first, tree check second, then SUBMITTING; a closed tree releases the slot and polls every minute

```text
	switch waitlisted, err := acquireSubmitQueue(ctx, rs, impl.RM, cg.SubmitOptions); {
	case err != nil:
		return nil, err
	case waitlisted:
		// This Run will be notified by Submit Queue once its turn comes.
		return &Result{State: rs}, nil
	}
	rs.CloneSubmission()
	switch treeOpen, treeErr := rs.CheckTree(ctx, impl.TreeFactory); {
	// ... (>10 min of tree-status errors: release queue, reset triggers, FAIL)
	case treeErr != nil:
		logging.Warningf(ctx, "tree-status check failed with: %s, retrying in %s", treeErr, treeCheckInterval)
		fallthrough
	case !treeOpen:
		err := parallel.WorkPool(2, func(work chan<- func() error) {
			work <- func() error { return impl.RM.PokeAfter(ctx, rs.ID, treeCheckInterval) } // revisit after 1 minute
			work <- func() error { return releaseSubmitQueue(ctx, rs, impl.RM) }       // give up the Submit Queue
		})
	default:
		if err := markSubmitting(ctx, rs); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		s := submit.NewSubmitter(ctx, rs.ID, rs.Submission, impl.RM, impl.GFactory)
		rs.SubmissionScheduled = true
		return &Result{State: rs, PostProcessFn: s.Submit}, nil
```

### X93. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/gerrit-plugins/git-numberer/+/refs/heads/main/src/main/java/com/googlesource/chromium/plugins/gitnumberer/Generator.java`:35-56

*Shows (SM):* X+1 on the same branch; @{#1} plus Cr-Branched-From when the destination ref differs

```text
  public static String childMessage(
      RevCommit expectedParent, String childCommitMessage, String destRef)
      throws GitNumberValidationError {
    checkNotNull(expectedParent);
    PositionFooters pfParent = PositionFooters.extract(expectedParent);
    if (!pfParent.errors.isEmpty())
      throw new GitNumberValidationError(pfParent.formatErrors(expectedParent));

    StringBuilder newMessage = MessageTweaker.copyAndModifyingFooters(childCommitMessage);
    // Post-condition: we are appending lines to last paragraph
    // and all prior footers like Change-Id are already in this paragraph.

    if (destRef.equals(pfParent.position.branch)) {
      PositionFooters.appendCommitPosition(newMessage, destRef, pfParent.position.number + 1);
    } else {
      PositionFooters.appendCommitPosition(newMessage, destRef, 1);
      PositionFooters.appendBranchedFrom(newMessage, expectedParent.getName(), pfParent.position);
    }
    PositionFooters.copyBranchedFrom(newMessage, pfParent);
    newMessage.append('\n');
    return newMessage.toString();
  }
```

### X94. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/infra/gerrit-plugins/git-numberer/+/refs/heads/main/src/main/java/com/googlesource/chromium/plugins/gitnumberer/CommitValidator.java`:172-202

*Shows (SM):* The verifier: one parent, X+1, lineage, and no merge commits

```text
    switch (commit.getParentCount()) {
      case 0:
        // First commit on an orphan branch must have just initial position.
        validateCommitFooters(commit, destBranch, PositionFooters.INITIAL_POSITION, null);
        return;
      case 1:
        RevCommit parent = commit.getParent(0);
        walk.parseBody(parent);
        PositionFooters pFooters = extractAndValidateParentFooters(parent);
        checkState(pFooters.position != null);
        if (destBranch.equals(pFooters.position.branch)) {
          // The same branch for parent and this commit, and the same lineage.
          validateCommitFooters(
              commit, destBranch, pFooters.position.number + 1, pFooters.branchedFrom);
        } else {
          ArrayList<BranchedFromValue> lineage = new ArrayList<>(pFooters.branchedFrom);
          lineage.add(
              new BranchedFromValue(
                  parent.getName(), pFooters.position.branch, pFooters.position.number));
          validateCommitFooters(commit, destBranch, PositionFooters.INITIAL_POSITION, lineage);
        }
        return;
      default:
        throw new GitNumberValidationError("merge commit " + commit.getName() + " not allowed");
    }
```

*Shows (SM):* CV's only use of the Auto-Submit label: the CL owner pays the full-run quota

```text
func quotaPayer(cl *changelist.CL, owner, triggerer identity.Identity, t *run.Trigger) identity.Identity {
	switch owner {
	case "":
		panic(fmt.Errorf("CL %d: empty owner was given: %q", cl.ID, owner))
	case identity.AnonymousIdentity:
		panic(fmt.Errorf("CL %d: the CL owner is anonymous", cl.ID))
	}
	mode := run.Mode(t.GetMode())
	cqv := t.GetModeDefinition().GetCqLabelValue()
	switch {
	case mode != run.FullRun && cqv != trigger.CQVoteByMode(run.FullRun):
		return triggerer
	case trigger.HasAutoSubmit(cl.Snapshot.GetGerrit().GetInfo()):
		return owner
	default:
		return triggerer
	}
}
```

```text
      footers = self.m.tryserver.get_footers() or {}
      cq_no_rebase = footers.get('Cq-No-Rebase', [])
      if any(v.strip().lower() == 'true' for v in cq_no_rebase):
        if self.m.cv.active and self.m.cv.run_mode != self.m.cv.DRY_RUN:
          raise self.m.step.StepFailure(
            'The Cq-No-Rebase footer is only supported for CQ dry runs, but '
            f'this build is part of a {self.m.cv.run_mode} run.'
          )
        allow_dry_run_reuse_only = self.m.cv.active
        kwargs.setdefault('gerrit_no_rebase_patch_ref', True)
```

```text
func UpdateTreeClosers(c context.Context, build *Build, oldStatus buildbucketpb.Status) error {
	// This reads, modifies and writes back entities in datastore. Hence, it should
	// be called within a transaction to avoid races.
	if datastore.CurrentTransaction(c) == nil {
		panic("UpdateTreeClosers must be run within a transaction")
	}

	// Don't update the status at all unless we have a definite
	// success or failure - infra failures, for example, shouldn't
	// cause us to close or re-open the tree.
	if build.Status != buildbucketpb.Status_SUCCESS && build.Status != buildbucketpb.Status_FAILURE {
		return nil
	}
```

### X127. `src/tools/mb/mb.py`:2454-2477

*Shows (TB):* FlattenMixins: left-to-right mixin expansion with gn_args string concatenation and single args_file

```text
def FlattenMixins(mixin_pool, mixins_to_flatten, vals, visited):
  for m in mixins_to_flatten:
    if m not in mixin_pool:
      raise MBErr('Unknown mixin "%s"' % m)

    visited.append(m)

    mixin_vals = mixin_pool[m]

    if 'args_file' in mixin_vals:
      if vals['args_file']:
        raise MBErr(
          'args_file specified multiple times in mixins for mixin %s' % m
        )
      vals['args_file'] = mixin_vals['args_file']
    if 'gn_args' in mixin_vals:
      if vals['gn_args']:
        vals['gn_args'] += ' ' + mixin_vals['gn_args']
      else:
        vals['gn_args'] = mixin_vals['gn_args']

    if 'mixins' in mixin_vals:
      FlattenMixins(mixin_pool, mixin_vals['mixins'], vals, visited)
  return vals
```

### X135. `src/docs/speed/perf_waterfall.md`:17-42

*Shows (PF):* The three-stage shape of the perf waterfall and why testers are not per-commit.

```text
## How It Works

The perf waterfall is split into three stages - builders, testers, and processors.

### Builders

For each commit to the Chromium repo, a Builder is invoked. The builder builds
Google Chrome, acquires test assets, and bundles everything up to be passed
along to Testers. We execute a builder for each platform we support. To ensure
we can keep up with the rapid flow of commits, we have a set of builders per
platform, each building a different commit.

### Testers

For each platform, we have a single tester job running continuously. Each run of
a tester covers the set of commits from the end commit of the previous
invocation to the latest _built_ commit. Each tester has one or more subdevices
(shards). The tester delegates a subset of tests to each shard and aggregates
high-level results (pass/fail, runtimes).

### Processors

Processors analyze the raw data generated by each Tester and convert it into a form that can be utilized
by the [Chrome Performance Dashboard](https://chromeperf.appspot.com/report).
For some jobs, this work is executed by the tester instead.
```

### X136. `src/docs/speed/perf_trybots.md`:3-21

*Shows (PF):* Pinpoint try jobs: with-and-without-patch on identical lab devices.

```text
Chrome has a performance lab with dozens of device and OS configurations.
[Pinpoint](https://pinpoint-dot-chromeperf.appspot.com) is the service that lets
you run performance tests in the lab. With Pinpoint, you can run try jobs, which
let you put in a Gerrit patch, and it will run tip-of-tree with and without the
patch applied.

[TOC]

## Why perf try jobs?

* All of the devices exactly match the hardware and OS versions in the perf
  continuous integration suite.
* The devices have the "maintenance mutex" enabled, reducing noise from
  background processes.
* Some regressions take multiple repeats to reproduce, and Pinpoint
  automatically runs multiple times and aggregates the results.
* Some regressions reproduce on some devices but not others, and Pinpoint will
  run the job on multiple devices.
* Each iteration runs both arms on the same device, eliminating confounding factors like across-device variability
```

### X137. `src/docs/speed/bisects.md`:3-9

*Shows (PF):* Why a perf-specific bisector exists and that it descends into DEPS-rolled repos.

```text
The perf tests on chromium's continuous build are very long-running, so we
cannot run them on every revision. Further, separate repositories like v8
and skia sometimes roll multiple performance-sensitive changes into chromium
at once. For these reasons, we need a tool that can bisect the root cause of
performance regressions over a CL range, descending into third_party
repositories as necessary. The name of the service that does this is called
[Pinpoint](https://pinpoint-dot-chromeperf.appspot.com/).
```

### X144. `https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/tools/build/+/1bb808e30ab7/recipes/recipes/pinpoint/builder.py`:101-125

*Shows (PF):* The public recipe behind Pinpoint's build quest: 'Perf on CQ' is named and Pinpoint-triggered builds are hidden from Gerrit (lines 127-130 then pin DEPS revisions instead of HEAD).

```text
def RunSteps(api: DEPS):
  # In Perf on CQ, if CQ triggers Pinpoint, the builds triggered by those
  # Pinpoint jobs will show up in Gerrit. We should not show them because
  # this should be part of Pinpoint workflow and be transparent to gerrit
  # end users.
  api.buildbucket.hide_current_build_in_gerrit()

  pinpoint_builder = api.buildbucket.builder_name
  perf_builder = _PINPOINT_MAPPING.get(pinpoint_builder)
  if perf_builder is None:
    api.step.empty(
      'no pinpoint mapping',
      status=api.step.INFRA_FAILURE,
      step_text=(
        'No pinpoint mapping is configured for {!r}.\n'
        'Please update pinpoint/builder.py'
      ).format(pinpoint_builder),
    )

  with api.chromium.chromium_layout():
    builder_id = chromium_types.BuilderId.create_for_group(*perf_builder)
    _, builder_config = api.chromium_tests_builder_config.lookup_builder(
      builder_id, use_try_db=False
    )
```

```text
    if group.updated + self._config.active_window <= update.now:

    elif group.created + self._config.triage_delay <= update.now and (
```

### X151. `src/docs/process/release_cycle.md`:8-15

*Shows (RC):* The current (2026) two-week cadence definition.

```text
Chrome ships a new milestone (major version) to the stable channel every two
weeks. The new milestone is developed on main for two weeks (beginning on
branch point for the previous milestone) before the milestone's branch is cut,
which is then stabilized for three weeks before being shipped to stable. Once
a milestone reaches stable, weekly updates (called refreshes) are shipped to
stable to deploy security fixes and keep Chrome's
[patch gap](https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/security-dev/c/fbiuFbW07vI)
short.
```

### X152. `src/docs/process/release_cycle.md`:19-26

*Shows (RC):* Extended Stable under the two-week cycle.

```text
Chrome Browser also maintains every fourth milestone branch for six additional
weeks by backporting important security fixes to create an extended stable
channel, where a new milestone is shipped every eight weeks. During the first
two weeks of this milestone, both stable and extended stable are shipped
identical releases; see the [channel lifecycle](#channel-lifecycle) to learn
more. The extended stable channel is only available to enterprises on the
Windows and Mac platforms, and can be enabled via enterprise policies. Weekly
refreshes are shipped to extended stable.
```

```text
| Branch Phase | Period Begins | Period Ends | Acceptable Merges Include Fixes For: |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| beta | M(X) Branch | M(X) Stable Cut | Non-functional issues for Finch-gated features (e.g. add metrics, fix crash), noticeable new regressions, any release blockers, any security issues, emergency string issues (.GRD changes) |
| stable | M(X) Stable Cut | M(X+1) Stable | Urgent new regressions (especially user reports), urgent release blockers, important security issues (medium severity or higher) requested by the security team |
| extended (if applicable) | M(X+1) Stable | M(X+2) Stable | Important security issues (medium severity or higher) applicable to any platform supported by Chrome Browser requested by the security team |

**NOTE:** Merge requests for changes introducing or modifying flag definitions will not be accepted for release branches; all flag changes must land before the branch cut date.
```

```text
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Merge-Request | ### | Release manager | Automation will review and either approve / reject directly, or pass the review to a release manager for manual evaluation |
| Merge | Pending | Issue owner | Issue owner should follow the instructions in the merge request and assign it to *merges@chromium.org* to begin review |
| Merge | Review-### | Release manager | Release manager will evaluate and either approve, reject, or request additional information within two business days |
| Merge | Approved-### | Issue owner | Issue owner should cherry-pick the fix to the appropriate release branch ASAP |
| Merge | Merged-### | None | N/A; merge has already been landed, no further work required for given milestone |
| Merge | Rejected-### | Issue owner | Issue owner should re-request a merge to escalate if they feel the merge was erroneously rejected and should be re-evaluated |
| Merge | TBD-### | Issue owner | Issue owner should evaluate if a merge is required, then remove *TBD-##* and replace it with *NA-##* (if no merge needed) or re-request a merge (if needed) |
| Merge | NA-### | None | N/A; merge is not required to the relevant milestone, no further work required for given milestone |
```

```text
class LandBranch(Step):
  MESSAGE = "Upload and land changes."

  def RunStep(self):
    if self._options.dry_run:
      print("Dry run - upload CL.")
    else:
      self.GitUpload(force=True,
                     bypass_hooks=True,
                     no_autocc=True,
                     set_bot_commit=True,
                     message_file=self.Config("COMMITMSG_FILE"))
    # TODO(crbug.com/1176141): This might need to go through CQ.
    # We'd need to wait for it to land and then tag it.
    cmd = "cl land --bypass-hooks -f"
    if self._options.dry_run:
      print("Dry run. Command:\ngit %s" % cmd)
    else:
      self.Git(cmd)

    os.remove(self.Config("COMMITMSG_FILE"))
```

```text
class FetchCandidate(Step):
  MESSAGE = "Fetching V8 lkgr ref."

  def RunStep(self):
    # The roll ref points to the candidate to be rolled.
    self.Git("fetch origin +refs/heads/lkgr:refs/heads/lkgr")
    self["candidate"] = self.Git("show-ref -s refs/heads/lkgr").strip()


class LastReleaseBailout(Step):
  MESSAGE = "Checking last V8 release base."

  def RunStep(self):
    last_release = self.GetLatestReleaseBase()
    commits = self.GitLog(
        format="%H", git_hash="%s..%s" % (last_release, self["candidate"]))

    if not commits:
      print("Already pushed current candidate %s" % self["candidate"])
      return True
```

### X173. `v8/tools/release/common_includes.py`:283-301

*Shows (RS):* Tagging by grepping the remote branch for the unique commit title with a fixed wait plan, then pushing the tag

```text
  def Tag(self, tag, remote, message):
    # Wait for the commit to appear. Assumes unique commit message titles (this
    # is the case for all automated merge and push commits - also no title is
    # the prefix of another title).
    commit = None
    for wait_interval in [10, 30, 60, 60, 60, 60, 60]:
      self.step.Git("fetch")
      commit = self.step.GitLog(n=1, format="%H", grep=message, branch=remote)
      if commit:
        break
      print("The commit has not replicated to git. Waiting for %s seconds." %
            wait_interval)
      self.step._side_effect_handler.Sleep(wait_interval)
    else:
      self.step.Die("Couldn't determine commit for setting the tag. Maybe the "
                    "git updater is lagging behind?")

    self.step.Git("tag %s %s" % (tag, commit))
    self.step.Git("push origin refs/tags/%s:refs/tags/%s" % (tag, tag))
```

```text
    if not self._state and os.path.exists(state_file):
      self._state.update(json.loads(FileToText(state_file)))

    print(">>> Step %d: %s" % (self._number, self._text))
```

```text
    hash_ = ''

    git_args = ['log', '-1', '--format=%H %ct']
    if commit_filter is not None:
        git_args.append('--grep=' + commit_filter)

    git_args.append(start_commit)

    output = _RunGitCommand(directory, git_args)
    hash_, commit_timestamp = output.split()
    if not hash_:
        return _EMPTY_VERSION_INFO

    revision = hash_
    pos = ''
    output = _RunGitCommand(directory, ['cat-file', 'commit', hash_])
    for line in reversed(output.splitlines()):
        if line.startswith('Cr-Commit-Position:'):
            pos = line.rsplit()[-1].strip()
            logging.debug("Found Cr-Commit-Position '%s'", pos)
            revision = "{}-{}".format(hash_, pos)
            break
    return VersionInfo(hash_, revision, pos, int(commit_timestamp))
```

*Shows (RS):* How refs/heads/roll (consumed by the Skia autoroller) is advanced from Chromium's current v8_revision

```text
def RunSteps(api: DEPS):
  api.gclient.set_config('v8_bare')
  update_result = api.v8.checkout()
  source_dir = update_result.source_root.path

  last_v8_revision = get_last_v8_revision(api)
  with api.context(
    cwd=source_dir,
    env={'DEPOT_TOOLS_UPDATE': '0'},
    env_prefixes={'PATH': [api.v8.depot_tools_path(source_dir)]},
  ):
    next_v8_revision = get_next_v8_revision(api, last_v8_revision)

    api.git(
      'fetch',
      'https://chromium.googlesource.com/v8/v8',
      'refs/heads/roll',
      next_v8_revision,
    )
    api.git(
      'push',
      'https://chromium.googlesource.com/v8/v8',
      f'+{next_v8_revision}:refs/heads/roll',
    )
```

*Shows (RS):* verify_version_tag: the branch HEAD is tagged with the version in v8-version.h if the tag does not already point there

```text
def verify_version_tag(api: DEPS, version_at_branch_head, build_results):
  with api.step.nest('Verify version tag'):
    commit_at_tag = get_commit_at_tag(api, version_at_branch_head)
    commit_at_head = api.v8.git_output(
      'show', '--format=%H', '--no-patch', 'HEAD', name='Commit at HEAD'
    )
    assert commit_at_head, 'Expected a checkout, but no head revision found.'
    if commit_at_head != commit_at_tag:
      # Tag latest version.
      if api.v8.dry_run:
        api.step('Dry-run tag %s' % version_at_branch_head, cmd=None)
      else:
        api.git('tag', str(version_at_branch_head), 'HEAD')
        api.git('push', REMOTE_REPO_URL, str(version_at_branch_head))
      build_results.performed_actions.append(
        "Tagged %s" % version_at_branch_head
      )
```
